headlines.title: CPI Hotter Than Expected: Is A Hike Back On The Table?
headlines.summary: September headline CPI came in hot at 0.6% month-over-month — that's the kind of print that puts a rate hike back on the table and sent the tape into a tailspin, triggering the KOSPI circuit breaker and the worst day for the S&P since July. Every rate-sensitive sector from tech to housing to long bonds gets repriced when the Fed's next move suddenly looks like 'up' instead of 'hold.' This is the root cause behind everything else ugly in this batch of news.

headlines.title: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt
headlines.summary: When CDS on a high-flying AI infrastructure name hit distress territory, that's not just a single-stock story — it's a flare gun going off over the entire leveraged AI build-out trade. CoreWeave's debt load is a proxy for how the Street is financing the AI capex boom, and if that credit starts cracking, the bid under Nvidia, the hyperscalers, and every data center REIT gets wobbly fast. This one's got contagion written all over it.

headlines.title: West Asia War: Riyadh Ravaged, Battles in Yemen, Iranian Mines Sink Ship
headlines.summary: Houthis hitting Saudi infrastructure and Iranian mines taking out ships in the Strait is the kind of escalation that puts an immediate bid under crude and a chill through global shipping and insurance markets. The IEA already scrambling to release diesel stocks tells you supply disruption risk is real, not theoretical. Energy names, tanker stocks, and defense contractors all feel this — and if the Strait of Hormuz gets dicier, you're talking about a macro shock that dwarfs the CPI print.
